---
name: quality-gate-adopt
description: Adopt, verify, or troubleshoot agentic-kit's quality-gate CLI in one repository, including its Git snapshot policy, Lefthook wiring, CI status, and optional model sites. Use for this CLI, not general code quality advice.
---

# Quality gate adoption

Read [the adoption guide](../../../docs/quality-boundaries.md) and the target project's intent, hook configuration, and existing gates. Scope the work to the requested repository. Do not change global hooks, MCP registration, credentials, fleet data, or other repositories as a side effect.

1. Establish the installed binary/revision, trusted external Git executable (`--git-bin` in CI), and existing hook commands. `quality-gate init --dir .quality-gate` creates a new directory only; if it already exists, inspect and edit deliberately. Validate the generated CUE/JSON policy, use provider `none`, and keep existing tests and scanners independent. Run `quality-gate doctor --policy-file .quality-gate/policy.json --format json` for local bootstrap diagnostics, then use committed policy after adoption. Its configuration-only result proves neither a snapshot verdict nor hook/CI invocation; follow the reported next actions without automatic policy repair or paid calls.
2. Merge the named Lefthook fragment (commit-msg checks the pre-commit policy over the index, avoiding Lefthook's empty pre-commit skip) without replacing commands. Inspect `lefthook dump`; `extends` may override an identically named command. Pre-push receives real Git stdin rows; only one Lefthook command can consume stdin natively. Show where all refs, raw-OID sources, new refs, deletions, and unavailable bases go. Prove the entire push preflights before model dispatch.
3. Observe an exact staged snapshot. Plant a violation in a disposable repo or temporary index and run the **installed hook**; prove a nonzero result, plus a missing-policy or malformed-input case. File existence and direct CLI success do not prove hook execution. Restore the fixture before handoff.
4. Pin enforcement to committed policy (`--policy-ref HEAD --policy-path .quality-gate/policy.json` locally; trusted base SHA in CI). Verify CI uses a pinned trusted binary and requires its unique status on a protected branch. For untrusted fork CI, do not pass secrets or run incoming code in `pull_request_target`.
5. Add model sites only when asked or justified by a concrete bounded question. Default to shadow, independent labels, and explicit per-invocation remote permission. A hold clear needs current full recipe/site-cohort/provider/resolved-model calibration; unknown/refusal/drift holds. Keep the default one provider batch per invocation unless the trusted project policy explicitly raises `model.max_batches`; failed attempts count and cache hits do not. A boundary without required rules/hold sites is unknown. Inspect unselected paths and required-receipt coverage. Never treat model clear as a waiver of structural, authority, evidence, or budget floors. Do not fabricate labels or claim model quality from a dry run.

Report the policy revision, snapshot, installed hook negative proof, CI status proof, retained gates, and any unverified layer. Exit `0` includes explicit observe; exit `1` is hold; exit `2` is unknown/invalid. If the target has no CI status or no installed hook proof, say adoption is incomplete. Do not install or mutate another project's wiring without that project's requested scope.
